negative_findings.description: No AML/regtech vendor (NICE Actimize, Oracle FCCM, SAS, ComplyAdvantage, Sanction Scanner, Tonbeller/FICO, etc.) was found publishing a named Montenegrin bank customer reference or case study.
negative_findings.result_summary: English and local-language searches returned only generic global 'top AML software' listicles and Croatian/Serbian SPNFT tools (SPNFT.hr, Potecon, SPINIFT) with no Montenegro bank reference.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: AML/regtech is a live spend area under EU-accession pressure, but the supply side is invisible in public sources. The vendor-reference route fails here and must be replaced by an alternative (bank annual reports, CBCG supervisory guidance, job ads naming AML tools).

negative_findings.description: No Montenegro-specific ATM hardware contract or customer reference found on Diebold Nixdorf or NCR Atleos channels.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches surfaced only global manufacturer strategy coverage and the Bankart/Diebold SEE middleware announcement; no Montenegro bank named.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: ATM fleet ownership in Montenegro appears to be intermediated by Payten rather than contracted directly with OEMs, which changes where the buying signal lives; the OEM channel is a weak collection point for this market.

negative_findings.description: Local-language vendor vocabulary for the supplier side is thin: Montenegrin/Serbian sources overwhelmingly use English-in-local terms ('core banking', 'POS', 'SoftPOS', 'processing') rather than native equivalents.
negative_findings.result_summary: Queries built on 'dobavljač', 'rješenje', 'implementacija', 'kartično poslovanje' returned mostly bank retail pages and generic portals; productive local queries were the ones mixing English product nouns with sr grammar.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Future collection must use mixed-language query templates ('banka + core banking + Crna Gora') rather than pure-sr translations, or recall will collapse.

negative_findings.description: No public core-banking platform attribution found for Hipotekarna banka, Adriatic Bank, Ziraat Bank Montenegro, Universal Capital Bank or Lovćen banka.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only regulator register entries and bank profiles returned; no vendor named a core system at any of these institutions.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The core-banking layer is the least visible part of the private-bank stack in Montenegro; digital-channel and ATM/POS layers are far better documented. Attribution here will need indirect fingerprinting (job ads, app metadata, SWIFT/ISO integration tenders, staff LinkedIn skill tags).

coverage_gaps.description: Core banking system attribution is unmapped for most of the 11 licensed banks; only digital-channel and ATM/POS suppliers are traceable.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated fingerprinting pass: bank job adverts (Temenos/Flexcube/Finacle/ASEE named as required skills), employee LinkedIn skill tags, bank annual-report IT investment notes, and SWIFT/ISO 20022 migration notices.

coverage_gaps.description: Recruitment and tender-adjacent sources (bank career pages, Montenegrin job boards, vendor local job ads) were not searched in this pass but are a first-principles high-yield route to technology stack disclosure.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a scouting pass over Montenegrin job boards (e.g. posao.me, zaposlise.me, HelloWorld regional) and bank 'Karijera' pages, filtered for platform names.

coverage_gaps.description: Scheme partner directories (Visa Ready, Mastercard Engage) were identified as pointer sources but their Montenegro-level filtering and ToS position were not verified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Manually exercise the region filters, record whether Montenegro is a selectable geography, and read the ToS before any automated extraction.

coverage_gaps.description: Foreign-owned banks (OTP/CKB, NLB, Erste, Addiko, Ziraat) may take technology decisions at group level, so the Montenegro-specific supplier trace is systematically incomplete.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add group-level vendor sources (OTP, NLB, Erste, Addiko procurement/IR pages and their group processors such as EGCP) and treat group announcements as inherited Montenegro signals.

coverage_gaps.description: No Montenegrin ATM/POS hardware reseller or maintenance provider besides Payten was identified; competitor presence (e.g. other regional service providers) is unmapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search the Montenegrin business register (CRPS) and MFIC/ICT Cortex directories for firms with payment-hardware NACE activity; check bank ATM branding and service stickers reported in local media.

brief: Montenegro's private-bank supplier ecosystem is dominated by one visible group: Asseco/ASEE, operating locally through e-mon (digital channels, with a published client list covering nine banks) and Payten (ATM/POS, claiming partnerships with 9 of 11 banks and hundreds of ATMs and thousands of POS terminals) — making vendor-side pages, not procurement portals, the primary intelligence channel. Beyond that spine, attribution thins out fast: digital-channel deals surface occasionally in trade wires (CKB–Misys/Finastra) and in bank customer notices that name outgoing and incoming platforms (Erste Podgorica migrating off Halcom to eMon OfficeBanking), while core banking and AML/regtech suppliers are essentially undocumented in public sources. The highest-leverage untapped route is technical and hiring fingerprinting — app-store bundle identifiers already reveal Asseco's mobile framework behind NLB ProKlik Crna Gora — combined with group-level vendor announcements from OTP, NLB, Erste, Addiko and Ziraat, since foreign owners often buy centrally. Local-language search is necessary but must mix English product nouns with Serbian grammar, since native supplier terminology is sparse.
